interpretation: After correcting the experimental structured-verdict protocol boundary, economical Luna implementer plus Terra reviewer completed the realistic multi-file Scenario 02 correctly in 2/2 repetitions with no recovery or remediation.
Across those matched repetitions it averaged about 65.7% fewer AI credits than released v0.2 while both were 2/2 correct.

The stronger Terra implementer is not monotonically better or cheaper: in one repetition its reviewer found real compatibility defects and required remediation, while the Luna implementations happened to preserve compatibility correctly in both post-fix repetitions.

Independent strong review remains valuable: Scenario 02 produced concrete reviewer-discovered compatibility defects, while the extra always-on coordinator and Worker B were not required for the successful economical repetitions.
The pre-fix economical failure demonstrates why deterministic protocol normalization should replace agent-level recovery for malformed-but-obvious structured verdict casing.
